Additional evidence from the affected session (`ses_28910d89cffepa6F6x95rQ8dmb`) that it became effectively unable to continue meaningful work:

- This session was running with the **Oh My OpenAgent plugin** enabled, so the final continuation spam should be treated as plugin-influenced behavior.
- The session did **not** end with normal assistant progress or a stable completion state. Near the end, it received repeated plugin/system continuation injections instead:
  - `2026-04-10T15:59:56.324Z`: `[SYSTEM DIRECTIVE: OH-MY-OPENCODE - TODO CONTINUATION]`
  - `2026-04-10T16:00:27.839Z`: `[SYSTEM DIRECTIVE: OH-MY-OPENCODE - TODO CONTINUATION]`
- Both late injections repeated the same directive:
  - `Incomplete tasks remain in your todo list. Continue working on the next pending task.`
- The last recoverable exported work state still showed unfinished work rather than convergence:
  - `=== Todos ===`
  - `[x] [completed] Inspect the current CV contact block markup and print styling`
  - `[x] [completed] Implement the homepage-style grouped phone/WhatsApp rows in the CV header`
  - `[-] [in_progress] Build and verify the CV page and exported PDF layout`
- Session metadata also shows this was a long, degraded run rather than a quick isolated failure:
  - `341 messages`
  - `988 transcript entries`
  - duration from `2026-04-10T10:27:58.023Z` to `2026-04-10T16:00:27.875Z`

So the strongest conclusion is:

- the **false PDF/capability mismatch** still looks like the most plausible OpenCode-core bug being fixed by this PR
- the **session becoming unable to continue further** is supported by evidence, but that terminal looping behavior appears to be **plugin-influenced** rather than something I can confidently attribute to OpenCode core alone

I’m adding this here because the practical user-visible failure was not just the bad PDF verdict — it was that after enough state churn, the session stopped making meaningful forward progress and collapsed into repeated continuation directives.

> Will this support a way to configure Bedrock to use AWS profiles without having to hardcode long-term AWS credentials? As an example, this is what I use for Claude Code (settings.json) and it works fine with temporary credentials (it even supports an auto-refresh mechanism)
> 
> ```
> {
>   "awsAuthRefresh": "op account get > /dev/null || eval $(op signin) && aws_mfa.sh -u <my.user> -m $(op item get  'AWS account'  --field type=otp  --format json | jq -r '.[0].totp')",
>   "env": {
>     "CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK": "1",
>     "AWS_PROFILE": "aws-dev",
>     "AWS_REGION": "eu-west-1"
>   },
>   "model": "eu.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6"
> }
> ```

Good question. The base already handles AWS_PROFILE — it reads it from the environment and passes it to fromNodeProviderChain, so the full AWS credential chain (profiles, STS, SSO, web identity, auto-refresh) works today without this PR. Your Claude Code pattern translates directly: just set AWS_PROFILE before starting opencode.

What this PR adds is two UI things on top of that:

1. An informational panel in the connect dialog that lists the supported env vars (AWS_PROFILE, AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK) — discoverability basically.
2. A separate flow to persist static IAM credentials (AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID / AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY) in auth.json for users who want UI-driven config rather than env vars.

For your use case — profiles with temp creds — you don't need the aws auth type at all, just set the env vars. The env panel is the part that's relevant to you.

In my case 
1, i deleted a model 
2. then restored it from backup

- the model refused to appear on the list of models inside the UI of LM studio
- model was not showing up via the API http://localhost:1234/v1/models

and when going to its download page it was showing the model as already downloaded
... and i could still load it manually

So deleting this
USER_FOLDER/.lmstudio/.internal/model-data.json 
did the trick (to make the restored-from-backup model to reappear):

**Alternatively this worked too:**
Changing the flag 
   **transient**: true
to 
  **transient**: false

Another option was to rename the parent folder of the model, this also made the model to reappear inside the ui and in the list via the API
